$comment: Hard gate for config/litellm-proxy.yaml (fleet-ops#8653). Nish 2026-09-28: no benching unless he says so. A failed row is never taken out of rotation: no bench list. Row cooldown_time: <=900 s is for ordinary transients. Values over 900 s, up to the 86400 s cap, are reserved for rows with a named, self-refilling wall (a daily or monthly quota that outlasts 900 s) - the row stays live, parked, and re-probes itself; each such row cites its issue in a comment (fleet-ops#8398/#9075). A row on openrouter.ai/api/v1 must set model_info.allowed_fails_policy.RateLimitErrorAllowedFails: 0, because its 429s are OpenRouter's named daily free-tier wall and the row has to park on the first one (fleet-ops#9248). Router-level cooldown_time holds a failed row for at most 60 s. Every model_list row must declare its cache capability: model_info.supports_prompt_caching (boolean) and model_info.cache_proof (non-empty string, date plus measured cached tokens or a doc link), because ~0% cache-read on four provider groups was 70% of uncached router tokens and no rule forced a new seat to say which case it is (fleet-ops#9365). A worker-group row whose supports_prompt_caching is false must set litellm_params.order: 2 so long sessions fall to it only as overflow (order filtering is applied after the cooldown filter in LiteLLM v1.98.0 router.py, proven by tests/test_router_order2_overflow.py). router_settings.redis_url is required: session_affinity pins live in the Router cache, and without Redis each of the proxy's 2 worker processes keeps its own pin, so a session flips between rows with no failure (fleet-ops#9015). LiteLLM v1.98.0 never reads a redis_url under general_settings.

allOf.$comment: fleet-ops#9365: a worker-group row proven unable to cache (supports_prompt_caching false) must sit at order 2, so long-session traffic stays on cache-capable rows and the false row serves only as overflow when order-1 rows are in cooldown.

fleet-ops#9248: a row on openrouter.ai/api/v1 is metered by OpenRouter's free-tier DAILY quota, so its RateLimitError must park the row on the first failure. Without RateLimitErrorAllowedFails the router-level default of 1 needs a second 429, and the wall leaks to the caller: 4 of 30 parallel worker-capable calls on 2026-10-04.

model_info.$comment: fleet-ops#9365: cache_proof is checked for presence and non-emptiness only, so the gate catches a missing verdict but does not read the text - 'unknown' would pass. That is deliberate: a pattern demanding a date and a token count would reject the legitimate 'cannot cache, here is the vendor doc' proof. What holds a hollow claim down is the proof line being a real measurement a reviewer can re-derive, and the probe behind it being quoted on the PR.
